name: Rowshon Ara Sarker
title: Community Organizer • Activist • Film Director • Writer
bio:
Rowshon Ara Nipa is an International Emmy Award-winning filmmaker, writer, and community organizer from Bangladesh, currently based in New York City. With over two decades of experience in storytelling, her work explores women's empowerment, social justice, cultural identity, and the resilience of working-class communities.

Challenging the patriarchal barriers of her upbringing, Nipa has dedicated her creative and professional life to amplifying marginalized voices. In 2004, she received an International Emmy Award for her journalistic work highlighting the lives of underprivileged children. Her acclaimed short film All Alone (2024) earned Best Screenwriter at the Berlin Indie Film Festival and recognition for women's empowerment at the Roshani International Film Festival, alongside six international festival selections.

Beyond filmmaking, Nipa works with DRUM – Desis Rising Up & Moving in New York City, organizing immigrant communities around housing, gender, and social justice. Drawing inspiration from her lived experiences and grassroots activism, she creates socially conscious cinema that bridges cultures, challenges injustice, and celebrates the transformative power of human resilience.
